messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a p95 decode spike after the merge that went out ~07:45 UTC. Baselines look fine in canary but prod p95 for short seqs jumped ~30%. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: I saw the alert in dashboards. p50 flat, p95 up for <=64 tokens. Looks like CPU and memcpy ops increased.

sam: timeline? which merge? can you paste the commit hash?

alex: Merge was 2002002801 (PR #3247) — fused-kv-prefetch + attention-kernel-selector tweaks. Commit: b3f9c7a.

jing: Reproduced locally on a small replica. If you run profile with --short-ctx workload, kernel chooser falls back to attn-fallback kernel for many steps, and we see repeated host->device memcpy spikes.

maria: I pulled perf flame for decode path (short seq):

```
- total 1000ms
  - token_decode 620ms
    - attn_fallback_kernel 320ms
    - memcpy_host_to_gpu 180ms
    - kv_prefetch_task 80ms
```

maria: kv_prefetch_task used to be ~15ms, not 80ms. Something in the prefetch loop got more aggressive and is doing larger memcopies + blocking calls.

sam: Interesting — the fused prefetch was supposed to merge small transfers to reduce PCIe ops. Could the change cause synchronous memcpy instead of async?

alex: I instrumented the code: the prefetch path now calls cudaMemcpy instead of cudaMemcpyAsync when the kernel-selector flag is set to favor fallback kernels (we pass a sync-flag in the merged path). Quick paste:

```cpp
if (kernel_selector == FALLBACK) {
  // old: async
  // cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, stream);
  cudaMemcpy(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); // new sync path
}
```

jing: That would explain the p99/p95 regressions on short sequences: each token decode waits for the copy. On long sequences latency amortizes.

sam: Can we confirm the CI perf run that merged this? I remember a flaky perf test got disabled.

deploy-bot: [CI] perf-canary/short-ctx: baseline=215ms, current=220ms (+2.3%) — threshold not exceeded.

maria: CI didn't catch it because the test used bigger batch sizes and merged the prefetch into a single bigger async copy — the pathological case is many tiny copies at low batch. Prod traffic has many single-user short completions.

alex: Bisect request: can someone confirm which sub-commit introduced the sync memcpy? I can try a local revert of the memcpy change.

sam: I already started a quick bisect. Preliminary: change came in patch 6 of the PR where we unified prefetch with kernel flags. If you revert that patch locally you get original timings.

jing: Patch that toggles async->sync guarded by kernel_selector was the culprit. I can open a hotfix PR to restore async copy for the prefetch path; keep the kernel-selector change separate.

maria: Patch idea: keep fused prefetch but ensure we always use cudaMemcpyAsync and cudaStreamSynchronize only when strictly necessary (e.g., fallback kernel case where kernel requires contiguous pinned buffer). Add an opt-in flag to allow the synchronous path during experiments.

alex: For immediate mitigation we should rollback b3f9c7a from main to stop new deploys. Rolling back will reintroduce the unmerged kernel-selector changes? We need to be careful.

sam: Revert would be minimal and quick. I'll prepare a revert PR and mark it as rollout-blocker.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback PR draft created: revert-b3f9c7a. Action: set canary hold.

maria: Also adding a focused perf test to CI: short-seq single-batch with trace to assert memcpy counts < 10 for 32 tokens. That should prevent this slipping.

jing: I'll prepare the hotfix with async memcpy in prefetch and run microbenchmarks. If green, we can merge hotfix and then do an A/B test of kernel-selector separately.

alex: One more ask: can someone push a lightweight telemetry change to count sync memcpy events/blocks in prod for next 6h so we can measure impact before/after revert? small metric: runtime.kv.sync_memcpy.count

sam: On it. will emit as a counter and add tags: commit=b3f9c7a hostpool=prod-west

maria: TL;DR: root cause = prefetch path switching to synchronous memcpy under new kernel-selector logic, causing per-token blocking copies for short sequences -> p95 spike. Fix = revert or restore async prefetch + add CI coverage.

alex: Thanks all. Action items: sam -> revert PR, jing -> hotfix async prefetch PR, maria -> CI perf test change, sam -> emit telemetry. If revert merges, hold canary then monitor p95.

sam: updating thread with PR links as they are created. :thumbsup:
